At the present time, TVA has no plans to develop additional pumped storage capacity. When the TVA system requires additional pumped storage capacity, it is probable that it would be developed at a site situated within the TVA service area, close to system load and supply. Further, if developed as an integral part of the TVA system, the Bad Creek Project would require the construction of new transmission lines to integrate the project with the TVA system.
The proposed Bad Creek Project would be a pure pumped storage development; i.e., no power would be produced from natural streamflow. The Bad Creek site has no potential value for flood control or irrigation, and hence there is no visible reason for the Corps of Engineers to consider its development. Comments received from Federal agencies in response to inquiries from the FPC did not indicate that Federal development of the site was being considered.
The Bad Creek Project would serve essentially the same load regardless of Federal or non-Federal construction. Federal development would not alter the environmental impacts of construction and operation. The direct cost of the project would be as much, possibly more, for the Federal Government; therefore, the only savings which might accrue from development would be attributable to lower financing cost. Tax revenues lost under Federal development would have to be recovered from other tax sources.
8.3 ALTERNATIVE PUMPED STORAGE SITES
The Applicant has identified 24 alternative pumped storage sites, of which the five most desirable were selected for further consideration. These five sites would also use Lake Jocassee as a lower reservoir. The FPC Staff made an independent study of 20 potential sites, not limited to the vicinity of the Jocassee Reservoir area. Many of the sites studied by the FPC Staff were eliminated from further study because cf (a) remoteness of the source of pumping energy; (b) excessively high capital cost to develop; and (c) severe environmental impact due to large reservoirs. Three sites as shown in Table 8-5 were chosen as the most desirable.
The Bad Creek Project would be capable of operating continuously at full load for 32 hours. For comparability, the alternative sites were sized to provide the same amount of energy in storage as Bad Creek. The unit costs were based on 1974 price levels. The Applicant's unit costs, based on a 1973 price level, were compared to unit costs estimated by others and appear to be reasonable.
